metric_convention: PURE PREFILL wall time: the chunk-loop time to build the KV cache for n_prompt tokens (the harness's PLOW_PREFILL_RESULT prefill_ms), EXCLUDING the first decode token. vLLM's ttft_ms (the comparison column) INCLUDES prefill + first-decode + scheduling, so plow_prefill_ms is the strictly-prefill lower bound of an equivalent TTFT.
run_mode: gemma4_sm120_chat: chunked PREFILL through the sm_120 persistent interpreter's prefill buckets, then greedy DECODE. Single .pkt, PLOW_UNISEG=1 (single-segment), buckets [128,512,1024,2048,4096,8192]+decode. Prompts are deterministic pseudo-random valid token streams truncated to length (prefill compute is shape-dependent, not content-dependent).

campaigns.change: FLASH_PREFILL scores S = Q.K^T now computed with mma.sync m16n8k16 (bf16, f32-acc) TENSOR CORES — the full BQ x BKV score tile in one tensor-core pass into smem, replacing the first-cut kernel's SERIAL per-KV-element warp_sum32 dot (the measured bottleneck). K is staged transposed for the mma B operand; the online softmax + P.V accumulation keep the validated FFMA lane-parallel O layout (a register-resident mma P.V is register-hostile at hd512 in this shared megakernel — the next A/B). campaigns.change: REAL cp.async pipeline for the prefill tiled GEMM (d_gemm/d_gemm_glu, op_gemm.cuh). T2 proved the staging was SYNCHRONOUS: pgm_stage_b did plain vectorized loads and cp.async.commit/wait operated on EMPTY groups. The blocker was the B (weight) operand being stored TRANSPOSED into smem ([k][n] scatter of 8 elems to 8 rows), which cp.async cannot express (it needs a contiguous 16B gmem->smem line). Fix: stage BOTH operands in their NATURAL, K-contiguous layout (A [m][k], B [n][k]) with cp.async.cg 16B lines (src-size operand zero-fills out-of-range M/N/K lines), and read the mma B fragment with ldmatrix.x2 NON-.trans instead of the in-tree .trans idiom. The non-trans B path was proven BIT-IDENTICAL to the old [k][n]+.trans path by a standalone probe (runtime/nvidia/experiments/t3_pipe_probe.cu: 0/2048 register mismatches, matches f32 CPU ref). Pipeline depth: plain GEMM rings 3 stages of (A,B); GEMM_GLU rings 2 stages of (A,Bg,Bu) — cp.async K-tile t+1(/+2) issued while the mma consumes tile t, commit_group/wait_group<STAGES-1> discipline. Because the mma operands are the same bf16 values in the same lanes, the f32 accumulation is BIT-EXACT vs T2: greedy tokens unchanged.

campaigns.change: L1 — cp.async KV-stream pipeline for the FLASH_PREFILL QK^T + P.V (op_attention.cuh d_flash_prefill, PLOW_NV_FA_PIPE=1). The T4 kernel staged each K/V tile with plain vectorized loads + a __syncthreads, so the mma stalled on the whole tile landing from HBM (the 128k HBM-KV-bound tail). T5 stages K NATURAL Ks[kv][hd] (was KsT[hd][kv] transposed) so it is cp.async-friendly and reads the QK B fragment with ldmatrix.x2 NON-.trans (the T3-proven bit-exact equivalent), and streams both K and V via cp.async.cg 16B lines. A full cross-tile double-buffer of BOTH operands (+33 KiB) does NOT fit the 99 KiB sm_120 opt-in cap, so the pipeline stays SINGLE-buffered and still overlaps both loads with compute by exploiting operand lifetimes: K is dead after QK so K[t+1] is prefetched right after QK[t] (overlaps softmax[t]+P.V[t]); V is needed last so V[t] loads at the tile top (overlaps QK[t]+softmax[t]); a last-tile empty commit_group keeps the wait_group<1> count uniform. BIT-IDENTICAL to T4 (same bytes, same lanes): GPU-verified LOGITS BIT-IDENTICAL (p_short) and same greedy tokens everywhere.

campaigns.verdict: MEASURED NEGATIVE for SPEED. fp8 w8a16 prefill is +0.4..+3.5% SLOWER than bf16 at every ctx. ROOT CAUSE: prefill GEMM is COMPUTE-bound, not weight-bound — large M (128..8192 rows) reuses each weight across many output rows, so the mma (not the weight stream) is the wall, and halving DRAM weight traffic buys nothing while the dequant convert pass adds overhead. This is the OPPOSITE of decode (M=1, bandwidth-bound, where the SAME fp8 weights win -10% TPOT). Consequence vs vLLM: plow fp8 prefill is 1.7-2.4x behind vLLM fp8 TTFT — WORSE than plow bf16 vs vLLM bf16 (1.4-2.3x) — because plow fp8 is slightly slower than its own bf16 while vLLM fp8 is FASTER than its bf16 (vLLM uses true fp8 tensor cores). THE REAL PREFILL fp8 LEVER IS w8a8 (fp8 mma.sync m16n8k32, 2x tensor throughput + per-row activation quant), which this w8a16 path is the correctness-complete foundation for. Committed opt-in (PLOW_FP8) at zero bf16 impact; it also enables the 10 GiB bf16-weight elision (neutral at 12B single-batch, matters for concurrency/larger models).

per_op_trace_16k.interpretation: The m16n8k32 2x-rate e4m3 mma cuts GEMM BODY cycles ~28% (not 2x): the tile stays 128x128 and the cp.async staging + pipeline + epilogue overhead is unchanged, and the new per-row QUANT_FP8 adds 6.2%. Net -17.4% total body cyc => -5..-16.5% wall. GEMM share drops 81%->71%; FLASH_PREFILL share grows 16%->20% and is the new co-bottleneck at long ctx (why the win shrinks -16.5%@4k -> -5%@128k: flash/HBM is a larger fraction there and w8a8 does not touch it).

campaigns.verdict: MEASURED POSITIVE for SPEED — the FIRST prefill lever in the campaign to BEAT plow bf16. w8a8 is -16.5%@4k, -11.6%@16k, -10.0%@32k, -7.8%@64k, -5.0%@128k vs plow bf16, exactly where T6 w8a16 (dequant-to-bf16) was NEGATIVE (+0.4..+3.5%): true fp8 tensor cores (2x rate) deliver where halving weight bytes did not, confirming the prefill GEMM is COMPUTE-bound. HOWEVER plow w8a8 does NOT beat vLLM fp8 TTFT: it is 1.56-2.29x behind (4k 1.75x, 16k 1.57x, 32k 1.87x, 64k 1.56x, 128k 2.29x) — about the SAME relative gap as plow bf16 vs vLLM bf16 (1.44-2.30x), because both engines gain similarly from fp8 (vLLM fp8 is -24% vs its bf16; plow w8a8 is -5..-16.5% vs its bf16). vLLM's tuned paged FA-3 + fused fp8 GEMMs keep the lead. The remaining gap is the FLASH share (now the co-bottleneck) + the unfused per-op launch/counter overhead + the un-double-buffered 128k flash, NOT the GEMM. Divergence is within the vLLM fp8 budget (plow drifts less than vLLM fp8 from its own bf16). Committed opt-in (PLOW_W8A8, prefill-only) at zero bf16/decode impact.
